assessment: Two proposed reuses of supplied resources merit bounded tests. Neither is established to achieve the pilot targets. Mixed-batch delays do not identify their cause, and overlapping widths do not identify the insertion problem.

openings.claim: Reuse the geometry recorded by existing cutting templates to make reusable board silhouettes for checking each order's complete partition set before insertion and packing.
openings.delta: Manufacturing geometry becomes a contents-checking surface: one position per required partition, including repeated shapes, could expose omissions and substitutions.
openings.prediction: A matched trial will detect more deliberately omitted or substituted partitions than the current check; separately timed checking and selection will reveal whether this reduces total work.
openings.probe: First verify template revisions against actual parts and independently confirmed component lists for accepted layouts. Use spare board for sample checking surfaces. Compare seeded-error detection and separately timed workflow stages across both workers and mixed layouts. Check exterior color against the order slip separately.
assumptions: Templates are explicitly available, but sufficient shape distinction and correct revision are unverified.
Fixture preparation must fit the fixed delivery date and 500-unit budget; added per-order material cost must remain at most 0.40.
This does not establish customer arrangement success.

openings.claim: Reuse the existing three-layout diagram as an order-specific placement reference by identifying the selected layout and explicitly pointing out the short partition's location.
openings.delta: An existing packing insert carries the customer's chosen arrangement and a targeted placement cue.
openings.prediction: With complete, correct parts, first-attempt short-partition placement will improve and requests for location help will decrease.
openings.probe: Verify that the incumbent diagram actually represents each accepted arrangement and current parts. Randomly assign the ten participants to existing versus revised diagrams; record unaided completion and short-partition placement before offering help. Treat results as preliminary; measure annotation time and cost.
assumptions: The diagram's existence is supplied; its coverage and economical editing method are unverified.
Product geometry, assortment, compartment counts, color and dismantling remain intact; preparation must respect budget and delivery constraints.
